1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. 21	+# Epic 8 Context: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management
22	+
23	+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
24	+
25	+## Goal
26	+
27	+Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data. This is the final build unit in the delivery order — it assumes every earlier unit (entries, auth, chat, export) already exists, since the dashboard has nothing to aggregate without entries and account actions rely on the auth session already established in F000.
28	+
29	+## Stories
30	+
31	+- Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts
32	+- Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State
33	+- Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing
34	+- Story 8.4: Logout
35	+- Story 8.5: Account Deletion
36	+
37	+## Requirements & Constraints
38	+
39	+- The evolution chart is computed fresh every time the settings screen opens — never served from a stale local cache — and must render correctly at exactly three entry-count scenarios: zero, one, and more than thirty. These counts are fixed and not re-tunable.
40	+- The narrative paragraph is a separate network call from the chart data, by design: the two must never be coupled so that a narrative failure cannot block or hide a chart that has valid data.
41	+- Aggregation must recalculate whenever a new entry is created anywhere in the app; because entries are immutable (never edited), invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create.
42	+- Account deletion is a hard, permanent delete of the account and all associated data (LGPD-driven) — not a soft delete or deactivation.
43	+- No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists for this delivery; both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same login/vault destination.
44	+- The persona selector shown on this screen is a cosmetic, non-functional placeholder only (an extension feature) — it must never appear to change assistant behavior.
45	+- Every acceptance criterion for this epic's FRs must pass as the primary success measure; no automated performance instrumentation is required beyond a manual spot-check against the product's general UI-latency thresholds.
46	+- Standard cross-cutting rules apply: no Clean Architecture layer violations, repository methods return `Either<Failure, T>` with no unmapped exceptions, and no visual value is hardcoded outside the design-tokens source.
47	+
48	+## Technical Decisions
49	+
50	+- Two features own this epic's work: a `dashboard` feature (chart + narrative aggregation/rendering) and a separate `account` feature (persona-toggle placeholder, profile edit, logout, delete account). Both are thin — standard layer-dependency and Either-error-channel rules apply, nothing feature-specific beyond that.
51	+- The dashboard screen uses the shared `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) view-state type, since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen — do not build a one-off state shape for it, and do not force the narrative fetch into the same `Resource<T>` instance as the chart (they are independent fetches, each can be its own `Resource<T>` if a second one is needed).
52	+- The dashboard is explicitly excluded from the local offline-cache pattern used by entries/chat — it has no `hive_ce` box and is never served from cache; each screen visit is a live fetch. Cache-invalidation behavior for the chart (recalculating after a new entry) is a presentation-layer concern owned by whoever builds this epic, not a shared local-cache mechanism.
53	+- This epic extends the minimal settings-screen stub already scaffolded earlier in the project rather than recreating the screen.
54	+- The 52px avatar shown here reuses the same avatar component already built earlier (previously only used at a 40px size) — do not reimplement it.
55	+- Charting uses `fl_chart` (already pinned for the project).
56	+
57	+## UX & Interaction Patterns
58	+
59	+- Dashboard empty/sparse states: zero entries shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary text at all (nothing to summarize, not a failure); exactly one entry shows a single bar with "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; more than thirty entries shows a 10-bar chart with the AI narrative paragraph below it.
60	+- Narrative-unavailable is a distinct visual state from the zero-entries empty state: when only the narrative call fails, the chart still renders normally and a clear "narrative unavailable" message appears in its place — never a blank space, never conflated with having no data.
61	+- Profile name editing: tapping the pencil icon beside the name switches it to an inline editable field and the pencil icon itself changes to a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon's meaning changes rather than just its color. Confirming saves and reverts to display mode; tapping away without confirming also reverts to display mode. There is no separate "edit profile" screen.
62	+- The account-deletion confirmation dialog uses a red (`colorError`) title — the only product-wide pattern where title color (not just an icon or badge) is the signal distinguishing an irreversible action from a routine interruption like session expiry (which uses a neutral title). This color must never be muted or reused for non-destructive confirmations.
63	+- The account-deletion dialog traps focus until dismissed or confirmed, reusing the same focus-trap overlay behavior already used by the session-expired overlay — no interacting with the scrim-covered screen underneath while it's open.
64	+- General overlay conventions apply: a scrim fades in first, the dialog/sheet sits at most one level deep over the base screen, and under reduced-motion settings the scrim/entrance animation is skipped in favor of showing the final state immediately.
65	+
66	+## Cross-Story Dependencies
67	+
68	+- Story 8.2's narrative text is fetched independently alongside Story 8.1's chart, but visually appears only once the chart from 8.1 is already rendering — 8.1 must ship the chart and its three entry-count states before 8.2's narrative/unavailable states are meaningful to build on top of.
69	+- Story 8.3 depends on the avatar component already built in an earlier epic; it must be reused at a new fixed size, not reimplemented.
70	+- Story 8.5's focus-trap dialog behavior depends on the same focus-trap pattern already implemented for the session-expired overlay elsewhere in the app; reuse it rather than building a second implementation.
71	+- Stories 8.4 and 8.5 both route to the same post-action destination (the login/vault screen) — keep that destination logic shared rather than duplicated between logout and account deletion.
72	+- The whole epic depends on entries existing (for the dashboard to have anything to aggregate) and on the auth session mechanism built in the foundation unit (for logout/deletion to have a session to end).

627	+
628	+/// Registers the `dashboard` feature into the project's single `get_it`
629	+/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `export_injection.dart`'s own shape. Must run
630	+/// after `registerEntriesFeature()` (`injection_container.dart`'s own call
631	+/// order, Code Map) since [DashboardCubit] depends on the shared
632	+/// [PendingEntryWriteTracker] that registration provides. No Hive box here
633	+/// (Boundaries/Never: "cache the aggregate", AD-15 exclusion).
634	+void registerDashboardFeature() {
635	+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardRemoteDataSource>(
636	+    () => DashboardRemoteDataSource(sl<ApiClient>()),
637	+  );
638	+
639	+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardRepository>(
640	+    () => DashboardRepositoryImpl(
641	+      remoteDataSource: sl<DashboardRemoteDataSource>(),
642	+    ),
643	+  );
644	+
645	+  // Boundaries — a `registerLazySingleton`, not a factory: long-lived, so
646	+  // its constructor subscription to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.
647	+  // confirmedWrites` stays live for the app's whole session (same
648	+  // rationale `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration gives). `dispose:`
649	+  // wires `close()` into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle, same convention
650	+  // every other long-lived cubit in this project already uses.
651	+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardCubit>(
652	+    () => DashboardCubit(
653	+      sl<DashboardRepository>(),
654	+      sl<PendingEntryWriteTracker>(),
655	+    ),
656	+    dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close(),
657	+  );
658	+}

671	+/// The dashboard feature's one remote data source — `dashboard-aggregate-
672	+/// get`, called by `x-cerne-function` name only (AGENTS.md), [period] sent
673	+/// as the one required `period` query parameter. Mirrors
674	+/// `ExportRemoteDataSource`'s own try/catch-to-`malformedResponse` shape
675	+/// for its decode step (RNF09).
676	+class DashboardRemoteDataSource {
677	+  DashboardRemoteDataSource(this._apiClient);
678	+
679	+  final ApiClient _apiClient;
680	+
681	+  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregateDto>> getAggregate({
682	+    required String period,
683	+  }) async {
684	+    final result = await _apiClient.get(
685	+      'dashboard-aggregate-get',
686	+      queryParameters: {'period': period},
687	+    );
688	+    return result.flatMap((json) {
689	+      try {
690	+        final data = json['data'] as Map<String, dynamic>;
691	+        return right(DashboardAggregateDto.fromJson(data));
692	+      } catch (error) {
693	+        return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString()));
694	+      }
695	+    });
696	+  }
697	+}

+# Epic 8 Context: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management
+
+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
+
+## Goal
+
+Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data. This is the final build unit in the delivery order — it assumes every earlier unit (entries, auth, chat, export) already exists, since the dashboard has nothing to aggregate without entries and account actions rely on the auth session already established in F000.
+
+## Stories
+
+- Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts
+- Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State
+- Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing
+- Story 8.4: Logout
+- Story 8.5: Account Deletion
+
+## Requirements & Constraints
+
+- The evolution chart is computed fresh every time the settings screen opens — never served from a stale local cache — and must render correctly at exactly three entry-count scenarios: zero, one, and more than thirty. These counts are fixed and not re-tunable.
+- The narrative paragraph is a separate network call from the chart data, by design: the two must never be coupled so that a narrative failure cannot block or hide a chart that has valid data.
+- Aggregation must recalculate whenever a new entry is created anywhere in the app; because entries are immutable (never edited), invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create.
+- Account deletion is a hard, permanent delete of the account and all associated data (LGPD-driven) — not a soft delete or deactivation.
+- No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists for this delivery; both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same login/vault destination.
+- The persona selector shown on this screen is a cosmetic, non-functional placeholder only (an extension feature) — it must never appear to change assistant behavior.
+- Every acceptance criterion for this epic's FRs must pass as the primary success measure; no automated performance instrumentation is required beyond a manual spot-check against the product's general UI-latency thresholds.
+- Standard cross-cutting rules apply: no Clean Architecture layer violations, repository methods return `Either<Failure, T>` with no unmapped exceptions, and no visual value is hardcoded outside the design-tokens source.
+
+## Technical Decisions
+
+- Two features own this epic's work: a `dashboard` feature (chart + narrative aggregation/rendering) and a separate `account` feature (persona-toggle placeholder, profile edit, logout, delete account). Both are thin — standard layer-dependency and Either-error-channel rules apply, nothing feature-specific beyond that.
+- The dashboard screen uses the shared `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) view-state type, since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen — do not build a one-off state shape for it, and do not force the narrative fetch into the same `Resource<T>` instance as the chart (they are independent fetches, each can be its own `Resource<T>` if a second one is needed).
+- The dashboard is explicitly excluded from the local offline-cache pattern used by entries/chat — it has no `hive_ce` box and is never served from cache; each screen visit is a live fetch. Cache-invalidation behavior for the chart (recalculating after a new entry) is a presentation-layer concern owned by whoever builds this epic, not a shared local-cache mechanism.
+- This epic extends the minimal settings-screen stub already scaffolded earlier in the project rather than recreating the screen.
+- The 52px avatar shown here reuses the same avatar component already built earlier (previously only used at a 40px size) — do not reimplement it.
+- Charting uses `fl_chart` (already pinned for the project).
+
+## UX & Interaction Patterns
+
+- Dashboard empty/sparse states: zero entries shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary text at all (nothing to summarize, not a failure); exactly one entry shows a single bar with "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; more than thirty entries shows a 10-bar chart with the AI narrative paragraph below it.
+- Narrative-unavailable is a distinct visual state from the zero-entries empty state: when only the narrative call fails, the chart still renders normally and a clear "narrative unavailable" message appears in its place — never a blank space, never conflated with having no data.
+- Profile name editing: tapping the pencil icon beside the name switches it to an inline editable field and the pencil icon itself changes to a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon's meaning changes rather than just its color. Confirming saves and reverts to display mode; tapping away without confirming also reverts to display mode. There is no separate "edit profile" screen.
+- The account-deletion confirmation dialog uses a red (`colorError`) title — the only product-wide pattern where title color (not just an icon or badge) is the signal distinguishing an irreversible action from a routine interruption like session expiry (which uses a neutral title). This color must never be muted or reused for non-destructive confirmations.
+- The account-deletion dialog traps focus until dismissed or confirmed, reusing the same focus-trap overlay behavior already used by the session-expired overlay — no interacting with the scrim-covered screen underneath while it's open.
+- General overlay conventions apply: a scrim fades in first, the dialog/sheet sits at most one level deep over the base screen, and under reduced-motion settings the scrim/entrance animation is skipped in favor of showing the final state immediately.
+
+## Cross-Story Dependencies
+
+- Story 8.2's narrative text is fetched independently alongside Story 8.1's chart, but visually appears only once the chart from 8.1 is already rendering — 8.1 must ship the chart and its three entry-count states before 8.2's narrative/unavailable states are meaningful to build on top of.
+- Story 8.3 depends on the avatar component already built in an earlier epic; it must be reused at a new fixed size, not reimplemented.
+- Story 8.5's focus-trap dialog behavior depends on the same focus-trap pattern already implemented for the session-expired overlay elsewhere in the app; reuse it rather than building a second implementation.
+- Stories 8.4 and 8.5 both route to the same post-action destination (the login/vault screen) — keep that destination logic shared rather than duplicated between logout and account deletion.
+- The whole epic depends on entries existing (for the dashboard to have anything to aggregate) and on the auth session mechanism built in the foundation unit (for logout/deletion to have a session to end).

+---
+title: 'Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts'

+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Configurações has no evolution chart yet; FR-09's "computed on demand, never stale" isn't met by anything in the codebase.
+
+**Approach:** New `dashboard` feature (already scaffolded empty) fetches `GET /dashboard/aggregate` fresh on every Configurações open, and a new chart section renders one of several states by total entry count: 0 → placeholder, 1 → single bar, >30 → condensed to 10 bars. The narrative paragraph is out of scope (Story 8.2).
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Call `dashboard-aggregate-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — fixed; no period selector exists anywhere in the product.
+- `DashboardCubit` is a `registerLazySingleton` that constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites`, recomputing on each event (entry created on another tab while this one stays mounted).
+- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `dashboardCubit.load()` unconditionally (beside the existing `clearStaleError()`) so every open is a live fetch, never the singleton's stale state.
+- States by `totals.count`: `0` → icon + "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; `1` → 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; `>30` → `bucketCounts` left-padded with leading zeros to length 10 (when shorter) *before* condensing to exactly 10 bars via 10 contiguous index chunks, summed `count`, remainder in the last chunk, no text; `2..30` → one bar per bucket as-is, no text (matrix gap, resolved per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed"). Bar height ∝ count / max count shown.
+- `DashboardAggregateDto` mirrors the full contract (`buckets[].{date,count,sources}`, `totals.{count,sources}`, same precedent as `ExportJobStatusDto`); domain `DashboardAggregate` exposes only `totalCount`/`bucketCounts`.
+- New visual tokens live only in `design_tokens.dart`, values read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard markup, reusing existing color/radius/elevation/spacing tokens wherever a pixel value already matches.
+
+**Ask First:** None. **Never:** render the AI narrative, a period selector, or cache the aggregate (AD-15 exclusion).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
+|----------|-------|------------------|
+| Zero entries | `count == 0` | Icon + "Comece a registrar..." |
+| One entry | `count == 1` | 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo..." |
+| >30 entries | `count > 30`, any `buckets.length` | Exactly 10 condensed bars, no text |
+| Mid-range | `1 < count <= 30` | One bar per bucket, no text |
+| Fetch fails | `Left(Failure)` | `ResourceError`, inline error text, no crash |
+
+</frozen-after-approval>
+
+## Code Map
+
+- `lib/features/dashboard/{data,domain,presentation}/` -- empty scaffold; all files below are new
+- `lib/core/resource.dart:10-32` -- `Resource<T>`, `DashboardCubit`'s state type
+- `entries_search_cubit.dart:20-21,140-170` -- emit/generation-guard template
+- `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart:80` (`confirmedWrites`) + `meus_registros_cubit.dart:29-32` (subscription template)

+**Execution:**

+**Acceptance Criteria:**

+## Spec Change Log
+
+- **Finding (blind-hunter + edge-case-hunter review, confirmed):** the frozen `>30` condensation algorithm ("10 contiguous index chunks, summed count, remainder in the last chunk") degenerates when `bucketCounts.length < 10`: `chunkSize = length ~/ 10 == 0`, so the first 9 chunks each sum an empty range (0) and the 10th chunk absorbs the entire total — renders as 9 invisible bars + 1 full-height bar, defeating the chart's purpose for a plausible user (concentrated activity across fewer than 10 distinct days while exceeding 30 total entries). The shipped implementation was 100% faithful to this frozen text; the defect was in the specified algorithm itself.
+- **Amendment:** added a left-pad step — `bucketCounts` is left-padded with leading zero-count entries to length 10 (only when shorter) *before* the existing chunking logic runs. `remainder in the last chunk` wording is otherwise unchanged. Routed to the human (AskUserQuestion) given the root cause sat inside `<frozen-after-approval>`; resolved in favor of a direct patch over a full revert-and-replan, per explicit human instruction to use technical judgment rather than follow the heavier protocol path.
+- **Known-bad state avoided:** a `>30`-entries chart collapsing into one meaningless giant bar for any user whose entries cluster into fewer than 10 distinct backend buckets.
+- **KEEP:** every other part of the shipped implementation (DI wiring, `Resource<T>`/generation-guard cubit shape, DTO/repository layering, `confirmedWrites` recompute, design tokens, test structure) is correct and must survive re-derivation untouched — only `_condense`'s input needs the left-pad step added ahead of it.

+
+**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
+- Open Configurações against 0/1/>30-entry fixtures and confirm the three chart states plus the inline error state on a forced failure. Covered by `dashboard_chart_section_test.dart`'s own widget-level equivalents (0/1/2..30/30/31/>30 with both `buckets.length` >= 10 and < 10, plus the forced-failure inline error state) in lieu of a device/simulator (AGENTS.md: none exists yet).
+
+### Round-2 review fixes (post-implementation)

+import '../../core/di/injection_container.dart';
+import '../../core/network/api_client.dart';
+import '../entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart';
+import 'data/datasources/dashboard_remote_data_source.dart';
+import 'data/repositories/dashboard_repository_impl.dart';
+import 'domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart';
+import 'presentation/cubit/dashboard_cubit.dart';
+
+/// Registers the `dashboard` feature into the project's single `get_it`
+/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `export_injection.dart`'s own shape. Must run
+/// after `registerEntriesFeature()` (`injection_container.dart`'s own call
+/// order, Code Map) since [DashboardCubit] depends on the shared
+/// [PendingEntryWriteTracker] that registration provides. No Hive box here
+/// (Boundaries/Never: "cache the aggregate", AD-15 exclusion).
+void registerDashboardFeature() {
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardRemoteDataSource>(
+    () => DashboardRemoteDataSource(sl<ApiClient>()),
+  );
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardRepository>(
+    () => DashboardRepositoryImpl(
+      remoteDataSource: sl<DashboardRemoteDataSource>(),
+    ),
+  );
+
+  // Boundaries — a `registerLazySingleton`, not a factory: long-lived, so
+  // its constructor subscription to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.
+  // confirmedWrites` stays live for the app's whole session (same
+  // rationale `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration gives). `dispose:`
+  // wires `close()` into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle, same convention
+  // every other long-lived cubit in this project already uses.
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<DashboardCubit>(
+    () => DashboardCubit(
+      sl<DashboardRepository>(),
+      sl<PendingEntryWriteTracker>(),
+    ),
+    dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close(),
+  );
+}

+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+
+import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
+import '../../../../core/network/api_client.dart';
+import '../models/dashboard_aggregate_dto.dart';
+
+/// The dashboard feature's one remote data source — `dashboard-aggregate-
+/// get`, called by `x-cerne-function` name only (AGENTS.md), [period] sent
+/// as the one required `period` query parameter. Mirrors
+/// `ExportRemoteDataSource`'s own try/catch-to-`malformedResponse` shape
+/// for its decode step (RNF09).
+class DashboardRemoteDataSource {
+  DashboardRemoteDataSource(this._apiClient);
+
+  final ApiClient _apiClient;
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregateDto>> getAggregate({
+    required String period,
+  }) async {
+    final result = await _apiClient.get(
+      'dashboard-aggregate-get',
+      queryParameters: {'period': period},
+    );
+    return result.flatMap((json) {
+      try {
+        final data = json['data'] as Map<String, dynamic>;
+        return right(DashboardAggregateDto.fromJson(data));
+      } catch (error) {
+        return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString()));
+      }
+    });
+  }
+}

After the user visits Configurações once, every later entry creation anywhere in the app triggers a background `dashboard-aggregate-get` network call even while the dashboard screen is not visible or mounted.   Based on a full read of the spec (`spec-8-1-on-demand-dashboard-aggregation-across-entry-counts.md`) and the complete diff, here is my audit.
  
  ## Findings
  
  - **`_condense`'s empty-`bucketCounts` defensive fallback never fires, defeating its own stated purpose for `totalCount > 30`**
    Violates: Spec Change Log → "Round-2 review fixes" bullet 2 ("Added a defensive fallback in `_populatedCard` for `totalCount > 0` with an empty `bucketCounts` (renders one bar for the whole total rather than an empty row)"), and the code's own cited rationale ("RNF09: never a blank/broken-looking screen over bad data").
    Evidence: In `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_chart_section.dart`, the guard is:
    ```dart
    } else if (totalCount > 30) {
      barCounts = _condense(aggregate.bucketCounts);
    } ...
    if (barCounts.isEmpty) {
      barCounts = [totalCount];
    }
    ```
    but `_condense([])` → `_pad([])` left-pads an empty list to `List<int>.filled(10, 0)`, and the chunking loop always emits exactly 10 elements regardless of input — so `_condense` can *never* return an empty list. For `totalCount > 30` with a contract-inconsistent empty `bucketCounts` (the exact scenario the fallback's own comment says it protects against), the `barCounts.isEmpty` branch never triggers; the chart instead renders 10 zero-height bars (`maxCount == 0` → every `heightFraction` is 0), i.e. a visually empty/broken-looking chart — precisely what the round-2 fix claims to prevent. The test suite only exercises this defensive guard at `totalCount: 5` (`dashboard_chart_section_test.dart`'s "defensive guard" test), never at `totalCount > 30`, so the gap went uncaught.
  
  - **Two dashboard layout gaps use the wrong design-token value (8px instead of the prototype's 12px)**
    Violates: Boundaries — "New visual tokens live only in `design_tokens.dart`, values read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard markup, reusing existing color/radius/elevation/spacing tokens wherever a pixel value already matches."
    Evidence: `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard block wraps the "Sua evolução" title and its card in `style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:12px;"`, and the non-empty card's bar row is `style="display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:8px;height:100px;margin-bottom:12px;"` (the gap between the bar row and the text below it is `12px`, not `8px`). The diff's `dashboard_chart_section.dart` uses `DesignTokens.spacingSm` (8, confirmed at `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:190`) in both spots instead:

    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),   // prototype gap is 12px, not 8px
    BlocBuilder<DashboardCubit, ...>(...),
    ...

  - **Consequence:** the last bar of the "more than 30 entries" chart can silently undercount, and the sum of all rendered bars can fall short of `totalCount`, for most real date ranges, with no test catching it.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a `_condense`-exercising widget test using a bucket count whose length is not a multiple of 10 (and already ≥ 10, so no padding is involved), e.g. 23 buckets with distinguishable per-bucket counts, asserting the final bar's `heightFraction`/underlying sum reflects the 5-element remainder rather than a 2-element `chunkSize` slice.
</agent-message>

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

## Review Results — Story 8.1 (on-demand dashboard aggregation)

All 4 layers completed (no failures). After normalizing, deduplicating, and verifying every finding against the actual code (not just the diff hunks):

**0 decision-needed · 9 patch · 1 defer · 2 dismissed as noise**

### Patch (unambiguous fixes)
1. **Blank-chart defensive guard never fires for its own target case** — `barCounts.isEmpty` is checked *before* `_condense` pads/chunks, but `_condense` always returns exactly 10 elements (never empty); the guard also misses the non-empty-but-all-zero case. Malformed `>30`-entry backend data still renders as an invisible chart — the exact thing this guard claims to prevent. [`dashboard_chart_section.dart:140-156`]
2. **Doc comment claims a `.clamp(0,1)` that doesn't exist** — `heightFraction` is computed as raw `count / maxCount` with no clamp. A negative bucket count (malformed data) would crash via negative `Container` height. [`dashboard_chart_section.dart:185`, `:275`]
3. **New VoiceOver announcement for dashboard fetch errors is completely untested** — the round-2 fix's whole point (announcing `ResourceError` via `_announce`) has no test; deleting it or inverting the condition would ship silently. [`account_settings_screen.dart:186-193`]
4. **`_condense`'s remainder-absorbing last bar — the entire reason for the round-2 spec amendment — is untested for any non-multiple-of-10 bucket length** (and the exact length-10 boundary). Current code is correct, but a regression to naive fixed-width chunking would silently drop real entries from the chart and no test would catch it. [`dashboard_chart_section.dart:223-248`]
5. **Two spacing values are 8px where the prototype specifies 12px** (title→card gap, bar-row→message margin) — verified directly against `cerne-prototype.html`'s `dashNotEmpty`/title-wrapper markup. [`dashboard_chart_section.dart:44,193`]
6. **Loading/error spinners have no semantic label** — inconsistent with every other accessibility fix made in this same commit. [`dashboard_chart_section.dart:71-89`]
7. **Misleading DI-ordering comment** — claims registration *call* order matters for correctness; both are `registerLazySingleton`, so only resolution order matters. [`dashboard_injection.dart`, `injection_container.dart:104`]
8. **Malformed-response tests only cover a top-level shape mismatch**, never a missing required nested field (`totals`, bucket `sources`) — the more realistic malformed shape for this nested contract. [test files]
9. **The `Expanded`+`SingleChildScrollView` overflow fix is never verified** under a constrained viewport or larger text-scale factor — its stated motivation is undemonstrated. [`account_settings_screen.dart:457-612`]

### Defer
- **`DashboardCubit`'s background recompute runs for the whole app session**, not just while mounted — every entry created anywhere triggers a live network call even with Configurações closed. This is exactly what the frozen spec's Boundaries mandates (`registerLazySingleton` + constructor-subscribe); fixing it means renegotiating frozen spec text, not a code defect.

### Dismissed
- `DashboardAggregate` hand-rolling `==`/`hashCode` instead of `ListEquality`/`freezed` — functionally correct, no convention violated.
- Claim that `DashboardCubit` could see an unhandled exception from `_repository.getAggregate` — verified false; `ApiClient.get` never throws (RNF09 codebase-wide invariant, confirmed by reading `api_client.dart`).

Findings will be written to `### Review Findings` in the spec file (inserted after `## Tasks & Acceptance`) and the defer item appended to `deferred-work.md`. Shall I proceed with that, then move to handling the patches?

- **Finding (blind-hunter + edge-case-hunter review, confirmed):** the frozen `>30` condensation algorithm ("10 contiguous index chunks, summed count, remainder in the last chunk") degenerates when `bucketCounts.length < 10`: `chunkSize = length ~/ 10 == 0`, so the first 9 chunks each sum an empty range (0) and the 10th chunk absorbs the entire total — renders as 9 invisible bars + 1 full-height bar, defeating the chart's purpose for a plausible user (concentrated activity across fewer than 10 distinct days while exceeding 30 total entries). file.content:
- Given `totals.count > 30`, then exactly 10 bars render regardless of `buckets.length`.

### Review Findings

- [ ] [Review][Patch] Blank-chart defensive guard (`barCounts.isEmpty`) never fires for its own target case — `_condense` always returns exactly 10 elements, and the guard misses the non-empty-but-all-zero case too [dashboard_chart_section.dart:140-156]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `heightFraction` doc comment claims a `.clamp(0,1)` that doesn't exist in code — a negative bucket count could crash via negative `Container` height [dashboard_chart_section.dart:185]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] New VoiceOver announcement for `DashboardCubit` `ResourceError` has no test — a regression would ship silently [account_settings_screen.dart:186-193]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_condense`'s remainder-absorbing last bar is untested for any non-multiple-of-10 bucket length (incl. the exact length-10 boundary) [dashboard_chart_section.dart:223-248]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Two spacing values use 8px (`spacingSm`) where the prototype specifies 12px (title→card gap, bar-row→message margin) [dashboard_chart_section.dart:44,193]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Loading/error `CircularProgressIndicator`s have no semantic label, unlike every other accessibility fix in this commit [dashboard_chart_section.dart:71-89]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Misleading DI-ordering comment claims registration call order matters for correctness; only resolution order does [dashboard_injection.dart, injection_container.dart:104]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Malformed-response tests only cover a top-level shape mismatch, never a missing required nested field (`totals`, bucket `sources`) [dashboard_remote_data_source_test.dart, dashboard_aggregate_dto_test.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `Expanded`+`SingleChildScrollView` overflow fix is never verified under a constrained viewport or larger text-scale factor [account_settings_screen.dart:457-612]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `DashboardCubit`'s background recompute runs for the whole app session, not just while mounted — every entry created anywhere triggers a live network call even with Configurações closed [dashboard_cubit.dart:26-29] — deferred, pre-existing: faithfully implements the frozen spec's explicit Boundaries directive (`registerLazySingleton` + constructor-subscribe); fixing it means renegotiating frozen spec text, not a code defect.
